notes:
CIRCUIT: 5sin20t V AC source driving three parallel branches off a top rail, all returning to a grounded bottom rail. Branch A = 2kOhm in series with 5uF; branch B = 20mH in series with 5kOhm; branch C = 100 Ohm alone. 7 components, 4 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1 = the top rail, y~372, x 210..667: V-AC top (2.0), 2kOhm resistor top (1.0), 20mH inductor top (0.0), 100 Ohm resistor top (3.0).
  n2 = the short vertical between the inductor bottom lead (518,435) and the top of the 5kOhm resistor (515,478): 0.1, 4.0. (traced edge e6, len 44)
  n3 = the short vertical between the bottom of the 2kOhm resistor (366,495) and the top plate of the 5uF capacitor (366,517): 1.1, 5.1.
  0  = the bottom rail, y~634, x 210..665, plus the stub down to the GND symbol: V-AC bottom (2.1), 100 Ohm bottom (3.1), 5kOhm bottom (4.1), 5uF capacitor bottom (5.0), GND (6.0).

CRITICAL SITES (explicit decisions):
  S0 (366,375) -> JUNCTION. Clean T: the 2kOhm column terminates on the top rail, no ink continues above it. The crossing reading would strand the whole 2kOhm/5uF branch off the source.
  S31 (514,635) -> JUNCTION. Four-way where the 5kOhm column crosses the bottom rail and continues down to the GND symbol. The crop shows a plain cross: no solder dot (dot=1.1) and no semicircular hop or sideways jog; the reported hop_score 3.6 is just the slight waviness of the hand-drawn rail. Junction is also the only electrically sane reading: as a crossing, GND + 5kOhm bottom would form one net and the rest of the bottom rail (V-AC bottom, capacitor bottom, 100 Ohm bottom) would be a floating return with no ground reference, splitting the return path of the circuit in two.
  S32 (361,636) -> JUNCTION. Clean T: the capacitor column terminates on the bottom rail. Crossing would strand the capacitor's bottom terminal on a one-terminal net.
  All other sites (S2, S4, S5, S9, S10, S11, S13, S14, S15, S16, S18, S21, S25, S26, S27) are non-critical: every one of them is a stroke of a handwritten value label ('20mH', '2KOhm', '5KOhm', '100 Ohm', '5uF', '5sin20t V') touching itself or brushing a component box. Left at their defaults; they touch no component terminal after the port/merge fixes below.

PORT / TERMINAL FIXES:
  #0 Inductor t1 -> port p2 (518,435). The tracer had assigned BOTH inductor terminals to 6px and 5px strokes of the handwritten '20mH' label sitting immediately right of the coil (p0 at (535,412), p1 at (534,420)), which shorted the inductor to itself (t0=t1=n1). p2 is the real bottom lead and carries the 44px wire down to the 5kOhm resistor.
  #0 Inductor t0: no port candidate exists for the top lead - the COCO bbox (x 498..531, y 376..432) swallows the entire top stub, so nothing survived box deletion. Verified in pixels (inkmap at 516,385): the top rail runs unbroken across y~371-372 and a solid vertical stroke descends from it at x~515-516 straight into the top of the coil. Expressed as merge ['0.0','2.0'], i.e. inductor top = V-AC top = top rail. Side effect: the small '20m' label blob that t0 nominally sits on is absorbed into n1; no other terminal touches it, so the grouping is unaffected.
  #1 Resistor(2k) t1 and #5 Capacitor(5uF) top node: the node between them is only ~5 px of surviving ink (edge e16, (366,495)-(366,499)) because the two annotated bboxes (resistor y 431..492, capacitor y 504..540) almost meet, so no port candidate was produced on either side. The tracer therefore parked 1.1 on a 6px stroke of '2KOhm' at (388,463) and 5.1 on a 7px stroke of '5uF' at (381,548), giving two bogus one-terminal nets. inkmap at (363,498) shows one continuous vertical pen stroke running from the resistor's bottom down into the capacitor's top plate at y~517 - they are genuinely one node. Expressed as merge ['1.1','5.1']. The two terminals nominally still sit on label-stroke edges, but the electrical grouping (exactly these two terminals, nothing else) is correct.

UNRESOLVED / CLASSES: none. All seven classes match the drawn symbols (coil = Inductor, three zigzags = Resistors, circle with a sine inside = V-AC, two parallel plates = Capacitor, hatched triangle = GND). No unconnected leads, no bridges dropped.
